Step 1: Set the stage—just get it on the table

Real talk: print the PDF. Grab crayons, chips, or even dried beans. No scissors? No problem. Literally put it in front of them and say, "Alright, teach me something." My son reacted weirdly—but weird in a good way, curious.

Step 2: Start small with 2+3 (the warmup equation)

How do you know when to step in and when to let them struggle productively? It's part intuition, honestly. An Institute of Human Development meta-analysis of 40 studies confirms moderate challenges produce the strongest learning. Too easy and they disengage; too impossible and tears follow. Validate their clever methods you didn't think of — crutches demystify ways out of mistakes. When children are allowed to honor their quirky counting tricks that sometimes swap two numbers but reach the same sum anyway, you get fewer meltdowns and way better outcomes overall.
